This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44097
* __->__ #39294 (merged)

CI is run only on the top PR, #44097, which contains both changes.

Merged into main as `ee30dc4d40993045273f0a90260db7efa302c214`. #44097 has been rebased onto this merge and now targets main directly.

Current head: `1adc6a6229fecca1b58cb56df6732c395ea65334`.

## Motivation

Joint FULL/SWA allocations can evict more cached prefixes than needed. FULL/SWA/Mamba allocations can fail despite recoverable capacity, or discard the entire cache before rejecting an impossible demand.

Seokwoo Song's original commits are preserved, rebased onto `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`.

## Modifications

- Stop allocation-driven eviction at a read-only sufficient-reclaim predicate; prepare and verify the physical layout at bounded phase boundaries.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte or ID bounds before eviction, and bound token/state reclaim quotas.
- Compute exact unsharded paged-extend demand for the unified SWA allocators while preserving conservative demand elsewhere.
- Update the dLLM KV-reuse test allocator to implement the paged-demand interface with the conservative default, fixing the CPU CI failure.
- Adapt the closed-move-gate regression to the current physical-page copy interface. Preserve main's SWA-preferred reclaim planning for storage-backed HiCache and decode disaggregation.

## Accuracy Tests

Latest main rebase: `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`. Both PRs replayed without conflicts, and all eight patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`. The exact combined top commit passed **87 tests / 211 subtests** on H200 (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130), covering dLLM KV reuse, prefill budget, joint reclaim, SWA page estimation, Mamba/Conv compaction and views (CPU and CUDA), and adjacent HiCache ordering/regressions. All changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Earlier CI follow-up, before this main rebase: reproduced the `get_extend_allocation_demand` failure in `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` before the correction. After updating the fake allocator in #39294, **66 tests / 162 subtests passed** across the dLLM KV-reuse, prefill-budget, joint-eviction, tri-pool reclaim, and SWA paged-extend suites on the H200 host (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130). All six dLLM tests passed. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Earlier validation before this main rebase:

- H200 host, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130: **220 tests / 1,050 subtests passed** across 14 allocator/cache files using Python TreeCore. These are CPU allocator tests.
- Freshly built current-main Rust TreeCore on the H200 host: **38 tests / 155 subtests passed** in the focused reclaim suite; session cases use the supported Python fallback. A separate probe asserted that the ordinary cache selected `RustUnifiedTreeCore`.
- With the compaction fix from #44097 applied in a separate combined snapshot on B300, Torch 2.14.1+cu130: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**, including the CUDA compaction cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Controlled real-allocator comparisons against unchanged main production code, with the same test fixtures, reproduced these results in both eager and lazy modes:

| Case | Main | This change |
|---|---|---|
| FULL/SWA, 6-token demand | Succeeds; evicts 5 cached tokens | Succeeds; evicts 3 |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 4-token demand | Fails | Succeeds; evicts 1 cached token |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 200-token impossible demand | Fails; evicts all 96 cached tokens | Fails; preserves all 96 |

The selected regression cases fail on main and pass on the candidate. Review checked quota semantics, deferred frees, page rounding, locked prefixes, changing move gates, pending reuse, and the compatibility of the rebase.

The FLOAT geometry predicates are sufficient certificates, not a complete feasibility solver. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU result is claimed. Historical serving evidence is retained below and is not validation of this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The controlled allocator comparisons above validate cache preservation and successful recovery, not serving throughput. No new serving-speed claim.

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add and validate regression tests.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [ ] Documentation: not applicable; no new user-facing API or configuration.
- [ ] Fresh model accuracy / serving performance benchmarks: not run for this rebase.

<details>
<summary>Historical description and validation before the current rebase</summary>

## Motivation

In unified-memory configurations, KV + SWA allocation can evict more prefix cache than necessary. Mamba + KV + SWA allocation can also fail despite recoverable joint capacity, or discard cached entries before rejecting an impossible request. This change bounds joint reclaim for these allocators to preserve reusable cache and recover capacity for feasible allocations.

## Modifications

- Stop the victim walk when the allocator’s sufficient reclaim predicate is satisfied, then prepare and check the actual allocation.
- Keep the per-victim feasibility predicate read-only and bound preparation to reclaim phase boundaries.
- Use the exact unsharded paged-extend demand where supported, retaining the conservative fallback for other allocators and sharded layouts.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte/ID bounds before eviction, preserving cached entries in those cases; bound remaining recovery attempts. This is not a complete feasibility solver for every FLOAT layout.

## Accuracy Tests

The focused three-file CPU suite passed **54 tests / 162 subtests** (23.73 seconds). Both lazy modes reproduced the allocator results below: two-pool demand 6 reclaimed 5 → 3 cached tokens; three-pool demand 4 changed failure → success; impossible three-pool demand 200 preserved all 96 cached tokens instead of evicting them. Baseline production code was unchanged; only test fixtures and regression files were supplied for comparison. These checks used Python TreeCore.

The current revision `3af4a9dd2bdb6cc0c5e7f27e3a09cbd5438fc647` additionally clarifies the two `evict_for_alloc` parameter contracts in docstrings only; executable ASTs are unchanged relative to the tested revision. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. All-files pre-commit also passed for the preceding API migration. GPU, Rust TreeCore, and serving results below remain historical results from the explicitly listed older revisions and were not rerun after this rebase.

Validation comparing upstream (`e17935820a47`) with this fix (`fb1d221b849d`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CPU, 14 files | 281 tests / 1,628 subtests passed |
| Rust TreeCore focused tests | 38 tests / 155 subtests passed |
| GPU allocator payload tests, RTX 5090 | 3 passed in both unit and serving environments; real KV and Mamba moves exercised |
| Formatting | All-files pre-commit passed |

| Actual allocator case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Two-pool demand 6 | 5 cached tokens reclaimed; allocation succeeds | 3 reclaimed; allocation succeeds |
| Three-pool demand 4 | Allocation fails | Allocation succeeds, reclaiming 1 cached token |
| Impossible three-pool demand 200 | Rejects after deleting all 96 cached tokens | Rejects while preserving all 96 |

These are controlled allocator cases, not serving throughput claims. The real-GPU pending-reuse race branch was not reached; no coverage is claimed for that branch. Request-owned SWA `WINDOW_FREE` events were also not observed in the serving workloads, including the supplemental longer-prefix lane.

| Serving comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) | 48/48 primary correctness sequences and 3,840/3,840 paired measured primary sequences match; mapping/concurrent output differences require the qualifications below |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) | 48/48 primary correctness sequences and 3,840/3,840 paired measured primary sequences match |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) | Both versions show the same two concurrent text variants; no universal token-ID parity or causal explanation is claimed |

Supplemental C2 collection is complete. A separate 128-output-token smoke test matched all 29 paired request sequences (Mellum 13, Inkling 16), with 58 requests, zero errors and zero reported retractions. This is limited longer-output coverage, not a throughput or quality benchmark. Output variability in other workloads is retained below.

<details>
<summary>Serving output comparisons, targeted diagnostics, and limitations</summary>

The primary Mellum and reduced Inkling correctness comparisons matched all 96 token-ID sequences. All 7,680 paired measured request sequences also matched across the 16 primary performance runs; the supplemental results and qualifications are reported separately below. The completed pressure mapping compared 636 requests across six paired configurations: 635 token-ID sequences matched. The one Mellum mismatch occurred at the 4K cap when a revisit retained 896 rather than 512 prefix tokens. It reproduced with caching enabled; all seven requests matched with caching disabled. A focused 48-request diagnostic reproduced the split and controlled retained-prefix depth: both versions produced identical 32-token outputs and full-vocabulary logits when matched at 512 tokens, and also when matched at 896 tokens. Changing depth from 512 to 896 reproduced the same output change on the baseline alone. Retained FULL/SWA KV matched seed bytes at prefix matching and immediately before each consuming forward. This localizes the observed reproducer to retained-prefix/compute-path sensitivity; the synchronizing diagnostic does not exclude unobserved races or establish output equivalence for other workloads.

Across two supplemental Mellum C2 pairs, 254/260 measured token-ID sequences and 46/52 warmup sequences matched. Both revisions produced all observed variants for the same input and retained-prefix depth, including the initially candidate-only warmup variant. All six measured differences correlated with request forward-entry order; that association alone is not an exact batch or kernel-level causal proof. A separate 232-request CPU-trace diagnostic found identical outputs in all three actual batch-sequence groups shared by both revisions. A fourth sequence group appeared only on the baseline, and all four attempted same-batch admission conditions were not realized. The diagnostic added 12 short warmups per server absent from the original C2 runs. CPU metadata and observed output prefixes do not prove actual GPU inputs, KV payload integrity, the final sampling decision, or race freedom. These descriptive C2 results are kept separate from primary performance measurements.

In fresh Qwen performance runs, one concurrent request produced the same two observed text variants in both versions; no candidate-only text variant was observed. Earlier token-ID triage also found within-candidate variation, and a candidate repeat matched both baseline runs. The allocator/scheduling/numerical cause remains unresolved. Performance text hashes are not complete token-ID parity coverage.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Fresh RTX 5090 / WSL measurements, using four Before/After pairs per workload. Historical serving numbers are excluded. Changes below are medians of paired changes; CPU is scheduler process time.

| Model / workload | Cached tokens per revisit, Before → After | TTFT p50 change | Output tokens/s change | CPU change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mellum (KV + SWA) / eviction threshold | 512 → 512 | -0.54% | +0.45% | -0.42% |
| Reduced Inkling (KV + SWA + Mamba) / eviction threshold | 0 → 512 | **-25.57% (-10.85 ms)** | +0.60% | -0.58% |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) / serial control | Unchanged | -0.24% | +0.90% | -0.87% |
| Qwen3.5-4B (KV + Mamba) / C4 control | Unchanged | -0.42% | +1.05% | -0.99% |

Mellum and Inkling use the preselected 8K-cap, oldest-first conditions at their baseline-calibrated eviction thresholds (9 and 12 cold requests). Inkling's revisit TTFT decreased in all four pairs (-23.35% to -26.49%). Whole-workload throughput changes were small, and cache reuse did not increase in every condition. A separate diagnostic replay at Inkling's threshold observed scheduled prefill work for the two revisits decrease from 2,048 to 1,024 tokens; this is the scheduler's extend-token count, not measured GPU FLOPs. None of the predeclared performance alerts triggered; this is not statistical equivalence or a general speedup claim. Qwen's output-variability limitation above remains.

Inputs are independently generated Python-style assignments. Alerts require a median throughput loss >5% or CPU increase >10%, or specified latency increases >5% and >2 ms, with at least three of four pairs adverse. Revisit TTFT p50 and phase E2E p50 are primary latency checks; p95 checks are exploratory. A triggered condition receives one bounded confirmation block; none triggered here. Follow-up to this PR: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33091

Fixes a case where FULL/SWA capacity checks pass individually, but the combined allocation still cannot fit in the shared pool.

@ch-wan following up on the review here.

I'm planning to rework this PR on top of #36729's allocator-owned design: keep its dispatch/reclaim planner as the base, and apply the remaining fixes for joint allocation that this PR tries to fix.

This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44097
* __->__ #39294 (merged)

CI is run only on the top PR, #44097, which contains both changes.

Merged into main as `ee30dc4d40993045273f0a90260db7efa302c214`. #44097 has been rebased onto this merge and now targets main directly.

Current head: `1adc6a6229fecca1b58cb56df6732c395ea65334`.

## Motivation

Joint FULL/SWA allocations can evict more cached prefixes than needed. FULL/SWA/Mamba allocations can fail despite recoverable capacity, or discard the entire cache before rejecting an impossible demand.

Seokwoo Song's original commits are preserved, rebased onto `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`.

## Modifications

- Stop allocation-driven eviction at a read-only sufficient-reclaim predicate; prepare and verify the physical layout at bounded phase boundaries.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte or ID bounds before eviction, and bound token/state reclaim quotas.
- Compute exact unsharded paged-extend demand for the unified SWA allocators while preserving conservative demand elsewhere.
- Update the dLLM KV-reuse test allocator to implement the paged-demand interface with the conservative default, fixing the CPU CI failure.
- Adapt the closed-move-gate regression to the current physical-page copy interface. Preserve main's SWA-preferred reclaim planning for storage-backed HiCache and decode disaggregation.

## Accuracy Tests

Latest main rebase: `ae28306a74fc9ba56daab9ccb06dcf45659f58af`. Both PRs replayed without conflicts, and all eight patches are unchanged by `git range-diff`. The exact combined top commit passed **87 tests / 211 subtests** on H200 (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130), covering dLLM KV reuse, prefill budget, joint reclaim, SWA page estimation, Mamba/Conv compaction and views (CPU and CUDA), and adjacent HiCache ordering/regressions. All changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Earlier CI follow-up, before this main rebase: reproduced the `get_extend_allocation_demand` failure in `test_dllm_fdfo_kv_reuse.py` before the correction. After updating the fake allocator in #39294, **66 tests / 162 subtests passed** across the dLLM KV-reuse, prefill-budget, joint-eviction, tri-pool reclaim, and SWA paged-extend suites on the H200 host (Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130). All six dLLM tests passed. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed.

Earlier validation before this main rebase:

- H200 host, Python 3.12 / Torch 2.13.0+cu130: **220 tests / 1,050 subtests passed** across 14 allocator/cache files using Python TreeCore. These are CPU allocator tests.
- Freshly built current-main Rust TreeCore on the H200 host: **38 tests / 155 subtests passed** in the focused reclaim suite; session cases use the supported Python fallback. A separate probe asserted that the ordinary cache selected `RustUnifiedTreeCore`.
- With the compaction fix from #44097 applied in a separate combined snapshot on B300, Torch 2.14.1+cu130: **61 tests / 201 subtests passed**, including the CUDA compaction cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Controlled real-allocator comparisons against unchanged main production code, with the same test fixtures, reproduced these results in both eager and lazy modes:

| Case | Main | This change |
|---|---|---|
| FULL/SWA, 6-token demand | Succeeds; evicts 5 cached tokens | Succeeds; evicts 3 |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 4-token demand | Fails | Succeeds; evicts 1 cached token |
| FULL/SWA/Mamba, 200-token impossible demand | Fails; evicts all 96 cached tokens | Fails; preserves all 96 |

The selected regression cases fail on main and pass on the candidate. Review checked quota semantics, deferred frees, page rounding, locked prefixes, changing move gates, pending reuse, and the compatibility of the rebase.

The FLOAT geometry predicates are sufficient certificates, not a complete feasibility solver. No fresh model-serving, full HiCache, or multi-GPU result is claimed. Historical serving evidence is retained below and is not validation of this head.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The controlled allocator comparisons above validate cache preservation and successful recovery, not serving throughput. No new serving-speed claim.

<details>
<summary>Historical description and validation before the current rebase</summary>

## Motivation

In unified-memory configurations, KV + SWA allocation can evict more prefix cache than necessary. Mamba + KV + SWA allocation can also fail despite recoverable joint capacity, or discard cached entries before rejecting an impossible request. This change bounds joint reclaim for these allocators to preserve reusable cache and recover capacity for feasible allocations.

## Modifications

- Stop the victim walk when the allocator’s sufficient reclaim predicate is satisfied, then prepare and check the actual allocation.
- Keep the per-victim feasibility predicate read-only and bound preparation to reclaim phase boundaries.
- Use the exact unsharded paged-extend demand where supported, retaining the conservative fallback for other allocators and sharded layouts.
- Reject demands proven impossible by byte/ID bounds before eviction, preserving cached entries in those cases; bound remaining recovery attempts. This is not a complete feasibility solver for every FLOAT layout.

## Accuracy Tests

The focused three-file CPU suite passed **54 tests / 162 subtests** (23.73 seconds). Both lazy modes reproduced the allocator results below: two-pool demand 6 reclaimed 5 → 3 cached tokens; three-pool demand 4 changed failure → success; impossible three-pool demand 200 preserved all 96 cached tokens instead of evicting them. Baseline production code was unchanged; only test fixtures and regression files were supplied for comparison. These checks used Python TreeCore.

The current revision `3af4a9dd2bdb6cc0c5e7f27e3a09cbd5438fc647` additionally clarifies the two `evict_for_alloc` parameter contracts in docstrings only; executable ASTs are unchanged relative to the tested revision. Changed-file pre-commit checks passed. All-files pre-commit also passed for the preceding API migration. GPU, Rust TreeCore, and serving results below remain historical results from the explicitly listed older revisions and were not rerun after this rebase.

Validation comparing upstream (`e17935820a47`) with this fix (`fb1d221b849d`):

| Check | Result |

| Formatting | All-files pre-commit passed |

| Actual allocator case | Before | After |

| Three-pool demand 4 | Allocation fails | Allocation succeeds, reclaiming 1 cached token |
| Impossible three-pool demand 200 | Rejects after deleting all 96 cached tokens | Rejects while preserving all 96 |

These are controlled allocator cases, not serving throughput claims. The real-GPU pending-reuse race branch was not reached; no coverage is claimed for that branch. <details>
<summary>Serving output comparisons, targeted diagnostics, and limitations</summary>

The primary Mellum and reduced Inkling correctness comparisons matched all 96 token-ID sequences. All 7,680 paired measured request sequences also matched across the 16 primary performance runs; the supplemental results and qualifications are reported separately below. The completed pressure mapping compared 636 requests across six paired configurations: 635 token-ID sequences matched. The one Mellum mismatch occurred at the 4K cap when a revisit retained 896 rather than 512 prefix tokens. It reproduced with caching enabled; all seven requests matched with caching disabled. A focused 48-request diagnostic reproduced the split and controlled retained-prefix depth: both versions produced identical 32-token outputs and full-vocabulary logits when matched at 512 tokens, and also when matched at 896 tokens. Changing depth from 512 to 896 reproduced the same output change on the baseline alone. Retained FULL/SWA KV matched seed bytes at prefix matching and immediately before each consuming forward.
